grh_05ae675b543d7d0d8a30.title: The Vanishing Elephant
paragraphs: A sacred white elephant disappears on the eve of an important festival, and Holmes discovers that the animal was secretly killed, cut into pieces and removed while an elephant call was sounded to preserve the illusion that it still lived. The reigning Maharaja is then murdered with poison placed in his eye drops and the elephant keeper is killed to prevent him from revealing the truth. Holmes confronts the Maharaja's brother, now the new ruler, as the man with the motive, medical knowledge and opportunity to commit both murders; beyond the reach of ordinary local law, he is ultimately threatened with the same legendary succession ritual he exploited.

[[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Basil Rathbone and Nigel Bruce. Other credited names include Edna Best as producer, Denis Green as writer, Anthony Boucher as writer, and Harry Bartell as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 30 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.bbd501bf461d302b|Petri Wines]] and [[org|org.bbd501bf461d302b|Petri Wines]].
This version is based on [[work|work.doyle.2f9ca4f462328758|The Engineer's Thumb]]. Arthur Conan Doyle is credited as author.

grh_05439b1dd88b23a99ebe.title: One Damn Thing After Another
paragraphs: A dramatization of correspondent Tom Treanor's One Damn Thing After Another recounts his comic and dangerous path from low-priority, often unauthorized war reporter to an accepted front-line correspondent. Treanor talks his way toward the fighting, borrows transportation, joins a bombing mission against orders, is repeatedly reprimanded or expelled from theaters of operation, and keeps mailing full newspaper stories when other correspondents cable theirs. The broadcast then steps outside the book to note that Treanor later covered Normandy for the Los Angeles Times and NBC and was killed in action, ending with a roll of newspaper and radio correspondents who had died covering the war.

This [[show|words-at-war|Words at War]] broadcast aired on November 14, 1944. [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes William Janney. Other credited names include Anton M. Leader as director, Gerald Holland as radio adaptor, and Jack Costello as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 29 minutes.
This version dramatizes [[work|work.words.b07b19e47f28eaf9|One Damn Thing After Another]]. Tom Traynor is credited as author and Gerald Holland adapted it for radio.

grh_05e1d2d98c234575c774.title: Battle at Tower Rock
paragraphs: Britt arrives in Tower Rock for the county fair and is maneuvered into judging a strawberry-preserve contest at the center of a bitter feud between Selma Bingham and Bessie Madden, a quarrel that has divided their husbands and much of the town. Rather than declare either woman the winner and deepen the fight, Britt awards the blue ribbon to preserves he ate at Gravy Gibson's lunchroom. Selma, Bessie, and their husbands instantly unite in outrage at Britt and walk off together, effectively ending their feud. Britt privately admits that Gravy's coffee had burned his tongue so badly he could hardly taste the entries anyway.
